reviews.comment: 208 is a difficult class, but Rogachev was excellent at helping us to understand the material. He does lots of examples in lecture and likes to work through a problem to show you how an equation is derived. He knows what he is talking about and will answer any questions students have about the material.

Rogachev is an excellent professor. 218 has difficult material, but Rogachev knows what he is talking about and is good about answering any questions from the class. He did a lot of examples in lectures to help us learn how to solve physics problems. He is awesome and I would definitely take him again!

Fantastic Prof! Second time I've had him, and this semester was even better. He loves teaching the material and wants his students to learn and be challenged. Don't expect a walk in the park with 208, but take it from Rogachev and you'll have a good instructor to guide you through everything.

Rogachev is a great prof. He knows his stuff and teaches it well. With him, Physics 208 didn't seem so bad! Only drawback to taking his class is the competitive component, worth 8% of the total grade, which is hard to get 100% in.
Clearly understands and explains the material well. If you have interest in physics his class is very interesting

Physics 218 is naturally a very hard course but Dr. Rogachev knows how to teach the material and has a true passion for it. He loves his students and wants to see them all succeed. His lectures consisted of 15-20 minutes of basic explanations then working out increasingly difficult problems. The honors points (8%) can be hard to achieve though.

Fantastic professor! Obviously cares about the material he teaches and whether his students learn. Class consists of briefly going over the general concepts and then going straight into challenging app. problems, which is what you want because the tests are all app. problems. Very challenging course, but take his class, study, and you can ace it.
Good prof, lots of work though. Knows the subject extremely well, and is pretty funny

Rogachev is a hilarious guy. His class is demanding but that's because of the material, not him.  I intend to take him next semester for 208. However, he primarily teaches by doing examples, so if you're not good at learning as you go, I would not recommend him.

Dr. Rogachev is an AMAZING physics professor. He is Russian, but his accent isn't hard to understand. He makes jokes about his time in Russia all the time and makes learning physics enjoyable. He goes over how to do problems in class and does a great job at making sure his students understand the material.

In the middle of taking his honors class, love him! He expects you to work hard for sure, but his lectures move at a good place, are very informative, and easy to understand despite his Russian accent. Very nice and understanding to talk to; easygoing. Make sure to put a lot of work in, because honors asks for more, but that's just the class.

He is a great prof. I did not learn as well from his as others because I did not read before class. His lectures pretty much consist of briefly going over the topics and then just doing a bunch of examples that get consistently harder. Read the first, maybe even second chapter before the first day of class and keep up with it.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He was a great lecturer but the class was hard. Don't expect to just go to class and pass. You NEED to do all the homework problems as they draw heavily on those for the test. Overall he was a likable guy

Brilliant professor. His accent doesn't get in the way and he is pretty clear in his explanations. He is very helpful in his office hours and is very interested in helping you do well. He does curve in the end but midterms are hard and doesn't curve those. If you do the homework and do extra problems on your own you'll do pretty well in his class.

Good prof, hard class. Has an accent, but is easy to understand and pretty charming. Go to lectures, do the Mastering Physics, be engaged during recitation, and attend tutoring of any kind. Seriously. There is no such thing as over-studying for a test in this class.

He's good at getting his point across and his accent was easy to understand. The tests get increasingly harder, but don't panic too much because there will be a curve at the end of semester. There are random clicker quizzes during lecture so make sure you get your clicker early and always come to class; those points add up!
He goes into great detail the exact way to solve problems. Asks for feedback and is responsive to questions. Genuinely cares about the class. Occasionally funny.

Didn't do well on my first two tests in his class so it's been a struggle to pass. His accent isn't impossible to understand. Often he works through a problem too quickly and assumes everybody understands what he is teaching. Not an easy class.
